### Current Trajectory Average Income at Year 20: $20.5K {#sec-current_trajectory_avg_income_year_20}

::: {.callout-note collapse="true" title="📊 Details"}

Average income (GDP per capita) at year 20 under current trajectory trajectory.

**Inputs**:

- [Current Trajectory GDP at Year 20](#sec-current_trajectory_gdp_year_20) 🔢: $188T
- [Global Population 2045 (Projected)](#sec-global_population_2045_projected) 📊: 9.2 billion of people

$$
\begin{gathered}
\bar{y}_{base,20} \\
= \frac{GDP_{base,20}}{Pop_{2045}} \\
= \frac{\$188T}{9.2B} \\
= \$20.5K
\end{gathered}
$$
where:
$$
GDP_{base,20} = GDP_0(1+g_{base})^{20}
$$
*✓ High confidence*

### Total Annual Decentralized Framework for Drug Assessment Operational Costs: $40M {#sec-dfda_annual_opex}

::: {.callout-note collapse="true" title="📊 Details"}

Total annual Decentralized Framework for Drug Assessment operational costs (sum of all components: platform + staff + infra + regulatory + community)

**Inputs**:

- [Decentralized Framework for Drug Assessment Maintenance Costs](#sec-dfda_opex_platform_maintenance): $15M (95% CI: $10M - $22M)
- [Decentralized Framework for Drug Assessment Staff Costs](#sec-dfda_opex_staff): $10M (95% CI: $7M - $15M)
- [Decentralized Framework for Drug Assessment Infrastructure Costs](#sec-dfda_opex_infrastructure): $8M (95% CI: $5M - $12M)
- [Decentralized Framework for Drug Assessment Regulatory Coordination Costs](#sec-dfda_opex_regulatory): $5M (95% CI: $3M - $8M)
- [Decentralized Framework for Drug Assessment Community Support Costs](#sec-dfda_opex_community): $2M (95% CI: $1M - $3M)

$$
\begin{gathered}
OPEX_{dFDA} \\
= Cost_{platform} + Cost_{staff} + Cost_{infra} \\
+ Cost_{regulatory} + Cost_{community} \\
= \$15M + \$10M + \$8M + \$5M + \$2M \\
= \$40M
\end{gathered}
$$

*✓ High confidence*

### Maximum Trial Capacity Multiplier (Physical Limit): 566x {#sec-dfda_max_trial_capacity_multiplier_physical}

::: {.callout-note collapse="true" title="📊 Details"}

Physical upper bound on trial-capacity multiplier from participant availability. Even with unlimited funding, annual trial enrollment cannot exceed willing participant pool.

**Inputs**:

- [Global Patients Willing to Participate in Clinical Trials](#sec-willing_trial_participants_global) 🔢: 1.08 billion people
- [Annual Global Clinical Trial Participants](#sec-current_trial_slots_available) 📊: 1.9 million patients/year (95% CI: 1.5 million patients/year - 2.3 million patients/year)

$$
\begin{gathered}
k_{capacity,max} \\
= \frac{N_{willing}}{Slots_{curr}} \\
= \frac{1.08B}{1.9M} \\
= 566
\end{gathered}
$$
where:
$$
\begin{gathered}
N_{willing} \\
= N_{patients} \times Pct_{willing} \\
= 2.4B \times 44.8\% \\
= 1.08B
\end{gathered}
$$
*~ Medium confidence*

#### Sensitivity Analysis

{{< include ../figures/sensitivity-table-dfda_max_trial_capacity_multiplier_physical.qmd >}}

:::

### dFDA Patients Fundable Annually: 23.4 million patients/year {#sec-dfda_patients_fundable_annually}

::: {.callout-note collapse="true" title="📊 Details"}

Number of patients fundable annually from dFDA funding at pragmatic trial cost. Source-agnostic counterpart of DIH_PATIENTS_FUNDABLE_ANNUALLY.

**Inputs**:

- [dFDA Annual Trial Subsidies](#sec-dfda_trial_subsidies_annual) 🔢: $21.8B
- [dFDA Pragmatic Trial Cost per Patient](#sec-dfda_pragmatic_trial_cost_per_patient) 📊: $929 (95% CI: $97 - $3K)

$$
\begin{gathered}
N_{fundable,dFDA} \\
= \frac{Subsidies_{dFDA,ann}}{Cost_{pragmatic,pt}} \\
= \frac{\$21.8B}{\$929} \\
= 23.4M
\end{gathered}
$$
where:
$$
\begin{gathered}
Subsidies_{dFDA,ann} \\
= Funding_{dFDA,ann} - OPEX_{dFDA} \\
= \$21.8B - \$40M \\
= \$21.8B
\end{gathered}
$$
where:
$$
\begin{gathered}
OPEX_{dFDA} \\
= Cost_{platform} + Cost_{staff} + Cost_{infra} \\
+ Cost_{regulatory} + Cost_{community} \\
= \$15M + \$10M + \$8M + \$5M + \$2M \\
= \$40M
\end{gathered}
$$
*✓ High confidence*

### Diseases Without Effective Treatment: 6.65 thousand diseases {#sec-diseases_without_effective_treatment}

::: {.callout-note collapse="true" title="📊 Details"}

Number of diseases without effective treatment. 95% of 7,000 rare diseases lack FDA-approved treatment (per Orphanet 2024). This represents the therapeutic search space that remains unexplored.

**Inputs**:

- [Total Number of Rare Diseases Globally](#sec-rare_diseases_count_global) 📊: 7 thousand diseases (95% CI: 6 thousand diseases - 10 thousand diseases)

$$
\begin{gathered}
N_{untreated} \\
= N_{rare} \times 0.95 \\
= 7{,}000 \times 0.95 \\
= 6{,}650
\end{gathered}
$$

**Methodology**: [@rare-disease-only-5pct-have-treatment]

### Global Opportunity Cost Total: $101T {#sec-political_dysfunction_global_opportunity_cost_total}

::: {.callout-note collapse="true" title="📊 Details"}

Total global opportunity cost from governance failures: health innovation delays ($34T), underfunded science ($4T), lead poisoning ($6T), migration restrictions ($57T). Sum: $101T annually in unrealized potential.

**Inputs**:

- [Global Health Opportunity Cost](#sec-political_dysfunction_global_health_opportunity_cost) 📊: $34T (95% CI: $20T - $80T)
- [Global Science Opportunity Cost](#sec-political_dysfunction_global_science_opportunity_cost) 📊: $4T (95% CI: $2T - $10T)
- [Global Lead Poisoning Cost](#sec-political_dysfunction_global_lead_opportunity_cost) 📊: $6T (95% CI: $4T - $8T)
- [Global Migration Opportunity Cost](#sec-political_dysfunction_global_migration_opportunity_cost) 📊: $57T (95% CI: $57T - $170T)

$$
\begin{gathered}
O_{total} \\
= O_{health} + O_{science} + O_{lead} + O_{migration} \\
= \$34T + \$4T + \$6T + \$57T \\
= \$101T
\end{gathered}
$$

**Methodology**: [@political-dysfunction-tax-paper-2025]

*? Low confidence*

### Percentage Military Spending Cut After WW2: 87.6% {#sec-post_ww2_military_cut_pct}

::: {.callout-note collapse="true" title="📊 Details"}

Percentage US military spending cut after WW2 (1945-1947, inflation-adjusted: $1,420B to $176B in constant 2024 dollars)

**Inputs**:

- [US Military Spending in 1947 (Constant 2024 Dollars)](#sec-us_military_spending_1947_annual_2024usd) 📊: $176B
- [US Military Spending at WW2 Peak (Constant 2024 Dollars)](#sec-us_military_spending_1945_peak_annual_2024usd) 📊: $1.42T

$$
\begin{gathered}
Cut_{WW2} \\
= 1 - \frac{Spending_{US,1947}}{Spending_{US,1945}} \\
= 1 - \frac{\$176B}{\$1.42T} \\
= 87.6\%
\end{gathered}
$$

*✓ High confidence*

:::

### Annual Funding from 1% of Global Military Spending Redirected to DIH: $27.2B {#sec-treaty_annual_funding}

::: {.callout-note collapse="true" title="📊 Details"}

Annual funding from 1% of global military spending redirected to DIH

**Inputs**:

- [Global Military Spending in 2024](#sec-global_military_spending_annual_2024) 📊: $2.72T
- [1% Reduction in Military Spending/War Costs from Treaty](#sec-treaty_reduction_pct): 1%

$$
\begin{gathered}
Funding_{treaty} \\
= Spending_{mil} \times Reduce_{treaty} \\
= \$2.72T \times 1\% \\
= \$27.2B
\end{gathered}
$$

*✓ High confidence*

:::

### US Discretionary Efficiency: 40.5% {#sec-us_fed_discretionary_efficiency}

::: {.callout-note collapse="true" title="📊 Details"}

US federal discretionary spending efficiency. What fraction of discretionary spending avoids direct waste (Cat 1 only: military overspend, corporate welfare, drug war, fossil/ag subsidies). ~41%. Some Cat 1 items (farm subsidies, tax expenditures) are technically mandatory/off-budget but are fungible policy choices.

**Inputs**:

- [Category 1: Direct Spending Waste](#sec-us_gov_waste_category_1_direct_spending) 🔢: $1.01T
- [US Federal Discretionary Spending (FY2024)](#sec-us_fed_discretionary_spending_2024) 📊: $1.7T

$$
\begin{gathered}
E_{US,disc} \\
= 1 - \frac{W_{cat1}}{Spending_{fed}} \\
= 1 - \frac{\$1.01T}{\$1.7T} \\
= 40.5\%
\end{gathered}
$$
where:
$$
\begin{gathered}
W_{cat1} \\
= W_{military} + W_{corporate} + W_{drugs} + W_{fossil} \\
+ W_{agriculture} \\
= \$615B + \$181B + \$90B + \$50B + \$75B \\
= \$1.01T
\end{gathered}
$$
*~ Medium confidence*

#### Sensitivity Analysis

{{< include ../figures/sensitivity-table-us_fed_discretionary_efficiency.qmd >}}

### US Governance Efficiency (GDP): 83% {#sec-us_governance_efficiency_gdp}

::: {.callout-note collapse="true" title="📊 Details"}

Total US governance efficiency: all 4 waste categories as share of GDP. 1 - ($4.9T / $28.78T) = ~83%. This broader metric captures direct spending waste, compliance burden, policy-induced GDP loss, and system inefficiency relative to total economic output.

**Inputs**:

- [US Government Waste (Total)](#sec-us_gov_waste_total) 🔢: $4.9T
- [US GDP (2024)](#sec-us_gdp_2024) 📊: $28.8T

$$
\begin{gathered}
E_{US,GDP} \\
= 1 - \frac{W_{total,US}}{USGDP} \\
= 1 - \frac{\$4.9T}{\$28.8T} \\
= 83\%
\end{gathered}
$$
where:
$$
\begin{gathered}
W_{total,US} \\
= W_{raw,US} \times US \\
= \$4.9T \times 1 \\
= \$4.9T
\end{gathered}
$$
where:
$$
\begin{gathered}
W_{raw,US} \\
= W_{health} + W_{housing} + W_{military} + W_{regulatory} \\
+ W_{tax} + W_{corporate} + W_{tariffs} + W_{drugs} \\
+ W_{fossil} + W_{agriculture} \\
= \$1.2T + \$1.4T + \$615B + \$580B + \$546B + \$181B + \$160B \\
+ \$90B + \$50B + \$75B \\
= \$4.9T
\end{gathered}
$$
*~ Medium confidence*

#### Sensitivity Analysis

{{< include ../figures/tornado-us_governance_efficiency_gdp.qmd >}}

{{< include ../figures/sensitivity-table-us_governance_efficiency_gdp.qmd >}}

### Category 1: Direct Spending Waste: $1.01T {#sec-us_gov_waste_category_1_direct_spending}

::: {.callout-note collapse="true" title="📊 Details"}

Category 1: Direct Federal Spending Waste. Actual federal budget allocations that could be redirected. Includes military overspend ($615B), corporate welfare ($181B), drug war ($90B), fossil fuel subsidies ($50B), and agricultural subsidies ($75B). Total: ~$1.01T annually. Solution: Budget reallocation.

**Inputs**:

- [Military Overspend](#sec-us_gov_waste_military_overspend) 📊: $615B (95% CI: $500B - $750B)
- [Corporate Welfare Waste](#sec-us_gov_waste_corporate_welfare) 📊: $181B (95% CI: $150B - $220B)
- [Drug War Cost](#sec-us_gov_waste_drug_war) 📊: $90B (95% CI: $60B - $150B)
- [Fossil Fuel Subsidies (Explicit)](#sec-us_gov_waste_fossil_fuel_subsidies) 📊: $50B (95% CI: $30B - $80B)
- [Agricultural Subsidies Deadweight Loss](#sec-us_gov_waste_agricultural_subsidies) 📊: $75B (95% CI: $50B - $120B)

$$
\begin{gathered}
W_{cat1} \\
= W_{military} + W_{corporate} + W_{drugs} + W_{fossil} \\
+ W_{agriculture} \\
= \$615B + \$181B + \$90B + \$50B + \$75B \\
= \$1.01T
\end{gathered}
$$

*~ Medium confidence*

### Efficiency Gap / Treaty Funding: 180:1 {#sec-us_gov_waste_vs_treaty_multiplier}

::: {.callout-note collapse="true" title="📊 Details"}

How many times the US government efficiency gap could fund the 1% Treaty. The efficiency gap represents capital that could fund transformative health research many times over.

**Inputs**:

- [US Government Waste (Total)](#sec-us_gov_waste_total) 🔢: $4.9T
- [Annual Funding from 1% of Global Military Spending Redirected to DIH](#sec-treaty_annual_funding) 🔢: $27.2B

$$
\begin{gathered}
k_{waste:treaty} \\
= \frac{W_{total,US}}{Funding_{treaty}} \\
= \frac{\$4.9T}{\$27.2B} \\
= 180
\end{gathered}
$$
where:
$$
\begin{gathered}
W_{total,US} \\
= W_{raw,US} \times US \\
= \$4.9T \times 1 \\
= \$4.9T
\end{gathered}
$$
where:
$$
\begin{gathered}
W_{raw,US} \\
= W_{health} + W_{housing} + W_{military} + W_{regulatory} \\
+ W_{tax} + W_{corporate} + W_{tariffs} + W_{drugs} \\
+ W_{fossil} + W_{agriculture} \\
= \$1.2T + \$1.4T + \$615B + \$580B + \$546B + \$181B + \$160B \\
+ \$90B + \$50B + \$75B \\
= \$4.9T
\end{gathered}
$$
where:
$$
\begin{gathered}
Funding_{treaty} \\
= Spending_{mil} \times Reduce_{treaty} \\
= \$2.72T \times 1\% \\
= \$27.2B
\end{gathered}
$$

### Wishonia Disease Cure Fraction (20yr, Full Implementation): 100% {#sec-wishonia_disease_cure_fraction_20yr_full}

::: {.callout-note collapse="true" title="📊 Details"}

Wishonia disease-cure fraction over 20 years under full implementation. Uses full trial-capacity scaling and applies an upper bound of 100% of untreated disease classes.

**Inputs**:

- [Diseases Getting First Treatment Per Year](#sec-new_disease_first_treatments_per_year) 📊: 15 diseases/year (95% CI: 8 diseases/year - 30 diseases/year)
- [Trial Capacity Multiplier](#sec-dfda_trial_capacity_multiplier) 🔢: 12.3x
- [Wishonia Military Reallocation Physical Max Share](#sec-wishonia_military_reallocation_physical_max_share) 🔢: 87.6%
- [Maximum Trial Capacity Multiplier (Physical Limit)](#sec-dfda_max_trial_capacity_multiplier_physical) 🔢: 566x
- [Diseases Without Effective Treatment](#sec-diseases_without_effective_treatment) 🔢: 6.65 thousand diseases

$$
\begin{gathered}
f_{cure,20,wish} \\
= \min\left(1,\frac{Treatments_{new,ann}\cdot k_{capacity,wish}\cdot 20}{D_{untreated}}\right)
\end{gathered}
$$

*✓ High confidence*

:::

### Wishonia Trajectory vs Current Trajectory GDP Multiplier (Year 20): 56.7x {#sec-wishonia_trajectory_gdp_vs_current_trajectory_multiplier_year_20}

::: {.callout-note collapse="true" title="📊 Details"}

Wishonia Trajectory GDP at year 20 as a multiple of current trajectory GDP at year 20.

**Inputs**:

- [Wishonia Trajectory GDP at Year 20](#sec-wishonia_trajectory_gdp_year_20) 🔢: $10.7 quadrillion
- [Current Trajectory GDP at Year 20](#sec-current_trajectory_gdp_year_20) 🔢: $188T

$$
\begin{gathered}
k_{wish:base,20} \\
= \frac{GDP_{wish,20}}{GDP_{base,20}} \\
= \frac{\$10700T}{\$188T} \\
= 56.7
\end{gathered}
$$
where:
$$
GDP_{wish,20}=GDP_0(1+g_{ramp})^3(1+g_{full})^{17}
$$
where:
$$
s_{mil,max} = Cut_{WW2} = 87.6\% = 87.6\%
$$
where:
$$
\begin{gathered}
Cut_{WW2} \\
= 1 - \frac{Spending_{US,1947}}{Spending_{US,1945}} \\
= 1 - \frac{\$176B}{\$1.42T} \\
= 87.6\%
\end{gathered}
$$
where:
$$
\begin{gathered}
f_{cure,20,wish} \\
= \min\left(1,\frac{Treatments_{new,ann}\cdot k_{capacity,wish}\cdot 20}{D_{untreated}}\right)
\end{gathered}
$$
where:
$$
\begin{gathered}
k_{capacity} \\
= \frac{N_{fundable,dFDA}}{Slots_{curr}} \\
= \frac{23.4M}{1.9M} \\
= 12.3
\end{gathered}
$$
where:
$$
\begin{gathered}
N_{fundable,dFDA} \\
= \frac{Subsidies_{dFDA,ann}}{Cost_{pragmatic,pt}} \\
= \frac{\$21.8B}{\$929} \\
= 23.4M
\end{gathered}
$$
where:
$$
\begin{gathered}
Subsidies_{dFDA,ann} \\
= Funding_{dFDA,ann} - OPEX_{dFDA} \\
= \$21.8B - \$40M \\
= \$21.8B
\end{gathered}
$$
where:
$$
\begin{gathered}
OPEX_{dFDA} \\
= Cost_{platform} + Cost_{staff} + Cost_{infra} \\
+ Cost_{regulatory} + Cost_{community} \\
= \$15M + \$10M + \$8M + \$5M + \$2M \\
= \$40M
\end{gathered}
$$
where:
$$
\begin{gathered}
k_{capacity,max} \\
= \frac{N_{willing}}{Slots_{curr}} \\
= \frac{1.08B}{1.9M} \\
= 566
\end{gathered}
$$
where:
$$
\begin{gathered}
N_{willing} \\
= N_{patients} \times Pct_{willing} \\
= 2.4B \times 44.8\% \\
= 1.08B
\end{gathered}
$$
where:
$$
\begin{gathered}
N_{untreated} \\
= N_{rare} \times 0.95 \\
= 7{,}000 \times 0.95 \\
= 6{,}650
\end{gathered}
$$
where:
$$
GDP_{base,20} = GDP_0(1+g_{base})^{20}
$$
*✓ High confidence*

### Wishonia Trajectory GDP at Year 20: $10.7 quadrillion {#sec-wishonia_trajectory_gdp_year_20}

::: {.callout-note collapse="true" title="📊 Details"}

Projected global GDP at year 20 under the Wishonia Trajectory. Model applies all Wishonia policy channels and redirects the full Political Dysfunction Tax non-health opportunity pool to highest-marginal-value uses. Health recovery is modeled separately through disease burden removal to avoid overlap. Military and non-health reallocation effects are ramped at 50% intensity for the first 3 years, then 100% for years 4-20, reflecting implementation lag. Military reallocation uses a physically demonstrated upper bound (post-WW2 demobilization) rather than an arbitrary policy cap.

**Inputs**:

- [Global GDP (2025)](#sec-global_gdp_2025) 📊: $115T
- [Baseline Global GDP Growth Rate](#sec-gdp_baseline_growth_rate): 2.5%
- [Wishonia Military Reallocation Physical Max Share](#sec-wishonia_military_reallocation_physical_max_share) 🔢: 87.6%
- [GDP Growth Boost at 30% Military Reallocation](#sec-military_redirect_gdp_boost_at_30pct): 5.5% (95% CI: 3.5% - 7.5%)
- [R&D Spillover Multiplier](#sec-rd_spillover_multiplier): 2x (95% CI: 1.5x - 2.5x)
- [Wishonia Disease Cure Fraction (20yr, Full Implementation)](#sec-wishonia_disease_cure_fraction_20yr_full) 🔢: 100%
- [Disease Burden as % of GDP](#sec-disease_burden_gdp_drag_pct) 📊: 13%
- [Global Science Opportunity Cost](#sec-political_dysfunction_global_science_opportunity_cost) 📊: $4T (95% CI: $2T - $10T)
- [Global Lead Poisoning Cost](#sec-political_dysfunction_global_lead_opportunity_cost) 📊: $6T (95% CI: $4T - $8T)
- [Global Migration Opportunity Cost](#sec-political_dysfunction_global_migration_opportunity_cost) 📊: $57T (95% CI: $57T - $170T)
- [Economic Multiplier for Healthcare Investment](#sec-economic_multiplier_healthcare_investment) 📊: 4.3x (95% CI: 3x - 6x)
- [Economic Multiplier for Military Spending](#sec-economic_multiplier_military_spending) 📊: 0.6x (95% CI: 0.4x - 0.9x)

### Disease Burden as % of GDP: 13% {#sec-disease_burden_gdp_drag_pct}

### Global Health Opportunity Cost: $34T {#sec-political_dysfunction_global_health_opportunity_cost}

::: {.callout-note collapse="true" title="📊 Details"}

Annual opportunity cost of slow-motion regulatory environment for health innovation. Murphy-Topel (2006) valued cancer cure at $50T (inflation-adjusted ~$100T in 2025). Longevity dividend of 1 extra year = $38T globally. PCTs could accelerate cures by 10+ years; NPV of 10-year delay at 3% discount = ~$25T. Conservative estimate: $34T annually in lives lost and healthspan denied.

### R&D Spillover Multiplier: 2x {#sec-rd_spillover_multiplier}

::: {.callout-note collapse="true" title="📊 Details"}

R&D spillover multiplier: each $1 in directed medical research produces $2 in adjacent sector GDP growth (biotech, AI, computing, materials science, manufacturing). Conservative estimate; military R&D spillover produced the internet, GPS, jet engines. Medical R&D spillover already produced CRISPR, mRNA platforms, AI protein folding.

#### Uncertainty Range

**Technical**: 95% CI: [1.5x, 2.5x] • Distribution: Normal (SE: 0.25x)

**What this means**: This estimate has moderate uncertainty. The true value likely falls between 1.5x and 2.5x (±25%). This represents a reasonable range that our Monte Carlo simulations account for when calculating overall uncertainty in the results.

*The normal distribution means values cluster around the center with equal chances of being higher or lower.*
